description: Dreamers is participating in the Casablanca NASA Space Apps Challenge. We created LUNAOPS, a web prototype for exploring lunar landing-site scenarios with an LRO/LOLA shadow-map layer, simplified Sun/Earth visibility, and adjustable comparisons. We care about lunar exploration, clear data visualization, and accessible tools. Its locations and scores are illustrative—not mission recommendations. We’re interested in lunar science, data analysis, web development, and design.
summary: LUNAOPS is an interactive prototype for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Lunar Landing Site Navigator.” Users can select example lunar south-pole site concepts and UTC dates, explore a simplified Sun/Earth visibility timeline, inspect power and communication proxies, compare site/date scenarios with adjustable priorities, and experiment with a resilience view. A separate explorer displays an archived LOLA-derived permanent-shadow map with its source and limitations. The project demonstrates how mission trade-offs can be explored transparently by students, the public, and analysts. Its site coordinates, rankings, and simulated outputs are illustrative and unvalidated; the map is context only. LUNAOPS is not a scientific instrument, a communications assessment, or a landing-site recommendation.
details:
LUNAOPS is an interactive prototype for exploring lunar south-pole landing-site scenarios. It brings candidate locations, a NASA LRO/LOLA-derived permanent-shadow map, simplified Sun and Earth visibility timelines, and adjustable weighted scenario comparisons into one dashboard. The map provides visual context only; the candidate locations, scores, and geometry outputs are illustrative, not validated mission data or landing recommendations.

The project aims to make factors relevant to lunar site exploration easier to understand and compare, supporting discussion by both technical and general audiences. Its creative approach combines lunar surface context with transparent, user-adjustable comparisons while clearly presenting data provenance and model limitations.

The frontend uses React, TypeScript, and Vite. A Python/FastAPI API supports local development, and Netlify Functions provide the hosted simulation and scoring endpoints. We considered NASA data attribution, uncertainty, terrain and communications limitations, and the risk of presenting prototype scores as operational guidance.
